summary: Huishan Lin is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Guowei Liu. Lin also studied under Mansheng, Miaoguan, and Ruying.
Huiwen Zhuang works in Buddhist studies. Zhuang earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Kirill Solonin, and studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Huiyu Zhang is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. Zhang was attested as a lecturer at Dongguk University in 1996.

Hung Wu is an art historian and sinologist who earned a master's at CAFA (1978–1980) and a PhD from Harvard (~1980–1987). He held professorships at Harvard (1990) and the University of Chicago (from 1994).
Hung-Yi Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Yang completed a PhD at the University of Sydney under doctoral supervisor Mark Allon (attested 2013).

Huston Smith (1919–2016) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago (~1940–1945). He taught at MIT (1958–1973), Syracuse University (1973–1983), and UC Berkeley (~1990–1999).
Huynh Kim Lan works in Buddhist studies and earned an MA in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2010), advised by Phra Suthithammanuwat and Veerachart Nimanong.
Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, studying under Kapila Abhayawansa.

Hwansoo Kim is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Kim held a professorship at Duke University (attested 2017) and serves as Professor of Religious Studies at Yale University (attested 2026).
Hyacinth Bitschurin (1777–1853) was a scholar of sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kazan Theological Academy and held a post at the Département asiatique (~1826–1853).

Hyakudai Sakamoto (1928–2020) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1951). He held positions at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1964–1994), Tokyo University of Pharmacy and Life Sciences, and the Open University of Japan.

Hyejeong Choi works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, completing a PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington (attested 2015). Choi was a visiting researcher at the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara in 2015.

Hyon Gak Sunim is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Yale (~1983–1987), the University of Freiburg (~1987–1988), and Harvard (~1989–1992), and trained under traditional teacher Seungsahn Haengwon (~1990–2004).

Hyoung Seok Ham specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied at the University of Virginia (2010) and earned a PhD from the University of Michigan under Madhav M. Deshpande (attested 2016).

Hywel David Lewis (1910–1992) was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Bangor University (~1928–1933) and Jesus College, Oxford (~1933–1935), later serving on the faculty at Bangor University (~1936–1955).

Hürelbaatar Ujeed specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Cambridge, where he held a post (attested 2010), and became Professor at Inner Mongolia University for Nationalities.

Ian Charles Harris (1952–2014) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge and Lancaster (PhD 1985), and held posts at Lancaster, St Hugh's College, Oxford, and the University of Cumbria.

Ian James Coghlan is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate in Asian Studies from La Trobe University (2004) and served as a research fellow at the Monash Asia Institute at Monash University (attested 2005).

Ian Kishizawa (1865–1955) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied at Saitama University and under traditional teacher Sotan Oka, later teaching Shunryu Suzuki and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani.

Ian Reader is a Japanology and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Leeds (1983). He held posts at the University of Stirling (~1989–1995), Lancaster University (~2003–2008), and the University of Manchester (~2008).
